summary: Three waves, each built around one main kind of risk and carrying the roadmap's safety gate for that risk inside the same plan: A reads mail (private data, by a reader that has no way out), B reads outside content (the open web through a helper that holds nothing, then photos and PDFs read by a parent's own agent), C lets Happy keep and schedule things (notes, reminders, and the calendar if it is Google). Putting mail first reverses the roadmap's own order, so wave A has to bring forward the firewall and the private-data controls; with those, mail alone fills one plan (my estimate: about 21 hours and 43 steps for Tony's inbox). Eighteen of the 42 items are in A to C; the other 24 are on the 'not in a wave yet' list with a reason each, because they rest on a family fact or a wish nobody has stated, or on a gate (local models, a paired device, acting outside the chat) that none of the three plans carries. Every wave fits one plan only in the simplified form of its cards, so each size is given both ways.

plan_size.basis: M0 was 50 steps and M1 was 49 steps in nine phases whose own estimates add up to about 20 hours, inside the roadmap's two weeks at 8 to 10 hours a week; that is about 0.4 hours a step plus a three-hour exit gate, and I count steps per phase at that rate. All figures below are my estimates, not measurements.

estimate.basis: My estimate, counted per phase at M1's rate: get ready 4 steps, 1.5 h; Google sign-in 7 steps, 3 h; firewall and scheduler switches 6 steps, 3 h; mail reader 11 steps, 6 h (2.5 h of that is the account check in code); morning text 6 steps, 3 h; paper and checks 4 steps, 1.5 h; exit gate 5 steps, 3 h. That is Tony's inbox only. Jordan's inbox adds 4 steps and 1.5 h; the envelope with T10 adds 3 steps and 1.5 h; with both the wave is 50 steps and 24 h, which is the most it can be. Taking S1 as well (no plugin yet) would save about 2.5 h. As the cards are written (two mail texts per parent with a sender list and a check on it, the Saturday tax job, the lookup, a job generator with a charter per job, the full self-check bundle, the stop plugin, the outage script) I estimate about 42 hours, which is two plans. notes: Mail first turns the roadmap's order around. The roadmap put web research before mail, so that the firewall and proxy were exercised on public data, and local models before any private data. With mail in wave A, the wave carries the roadmap's private-data gate (S3) in the form Tony's choices allow. Two of its lines cannot hold as written and need recording as changed: 'mail on a local model only' becomes 'the reader is pinned to one cloud model with storage off and no fallback', and 'the reader makes no network calls' becomes 'the reader has no network tool, the firewall shows the connector reaching Google only, and planted mail causes nothing but the text'.

Wave A is full with mail alone. About 21 hours and 43 steps for Tony's inbox, and 24 hours and 50 steps with Jordan's inbox and the envelope. Nothing else fits beside it, which is why web reading, photos and the calendar are in later waves. It also has a fixed eight-day wait for the sign-in test.

'Did I get an email about X?' goes live in wave B, not A. In A the mail reader is exactly the roadmap's shape (its only output is the scheduled text) and the parents' own agents stay as M1 signed them off. The lookup shares its hand-off test (T4) with the web helper, and the test its own card requires (a seeded mail must not cause a hand-off to the helper) only means something once the helper exists. If Tony wants it in A: about 2.5 hours more, which leaves room for Jordan's inbox or the envelope but not both, and the seeded-mail test is run again in B before the helper goes live.

The riskiest combination in A to C appears at the end of wave B: a parent's own agent can then ask the mail reader for mail and can hand a task to a helper that fetches any public address. Only a prompt rule and tests stand between the two, and the roadmap itself calls that hand-off its one remaining leak path. If Tony wants a harder line, the cheapest one is to leave the lookup off and keep mail as the morning text only.

I kept the roadmap's account check in code in wave A (one small plugin, one rule), where simplification S1 would build it later. It costs about 2.5 hours. If T5 shows the check is not called for connector tools, wave A runs on one layer (tool permissions, an explicit deny and two tests) and Tony should accept that in writing.

Wave B's gate has three open points for Tony. The proxy: about 4.5 hours to build, or a written waiver for the plain page-fetch tool. The firewall: the tight rule wave A puts on the gateway has to be widened once Happy fetches pages; the mail connector's rule stays tight. The Prompt Guard tripwire in the roadmap's S2: no card builds it and it needs a classifier running on the Mac, so it is either waived or scheduled with local models.

Wave B adds two kinds of outside content, not one: web pages read by a helper that holds nothing, and photos and PDFs read by the agent that holds a parent's chat history and can reach mail. Each goes live in its own phase after its own planted-content test. Wave A and wave C also add more than one kind (listed under new_risks), each in its own phase after its own check.

Eighteen of the 42 items are in A to C and 24 are not in a wave yet. That is the result of two rules, not of preference: a wave is not built on something Tony never said, and a wave must be one plan. If Tony says yes to several of the 24, they group by risk into further plans, because A to C have no room: 'Happy acts outside the chat' (the Reminders lists F030, email to the asker F049, the calendar write in F010, printing F080, lights and speakers F076), which needs the roadmap's recipient test and an approval in code first; 'a paired device' (MAC-04 first, then OCL-01 or MAC-02); and the kids' agent after local models.

Tony's two examples of advanced abilities, controlling a computer and a connected idle iPhone, are not in A to C. Each adds a kind of risk no earlier wave has (a paired device), the screen-control card has no chore named for it, and whether a spare iPhone exists is not on record. Under the roadmap's rule they are a wave of their own after C.

Wave C is the most conditional. Only notes (F041) is unconditional; reminders need Q6, the calendar phases need Q4, the facts and handbook phases need Q2 and Q10. With every answer yes it is about 22 hours. If the shared calendar is not Google, about 4.5 hours are free, and F030 or F049 could take that room after their own questions and tests.
Reminders are for Tony only unless he changes his 'no need' answer (Q9), so in wave C Jordan notices notes, and calendar answers if they are built, but not reminders.

Several cards ship in a smaller form than written, and the wave sizes depend on it: mail as one morning text with a school section (S6), jobs as three switches and one script (S9), operator cards as one check and paper (S14), photos as one switch and one test (S7), the trip planner without the billed place lookup (S13), one evening text (S10), dates into reminders only (S11). None of these has been confirmed by Tony. If he rejects S6, S9 or S14, wave A is about 42 hours and has to be split.

All hours and step counts are my estimates from counting steps at M1's rate. Nothing in the three waves has been tried on the Mac; the tests T1 to T8 and T10 are placed in the phases where their answers are needed, and a failed test changes the plan at that point (the fallbacks are named in the phases). T9 is not run in A to C because its only card, F030, is not in a wave.
